decisions.statement: Every unit akasha has installed is weighed against the text its page states.
A unit whose text is already what its page states is left alone and said nothing about.
A unit whose text drifted is written as the page states it.
systemd is told to read the units again where any unit was written.
What starts a service, arms a timer and moves the kind's tree is the deploy naming that kind.
A unit whose installed text could not be read is written as its page states it.
The tree a unit's run is spelled under is the tree the installed units already name.
A unit naming a path that tree has not got is left as the installed one is.
The deploy that moves the tree writes that unit, so the two move together.
A systemctl that refuses is said as wrong rather than thrown.
A reload that refuses leaves the units written.
Nothing here rules on how long a service has been up.
Nothing here installs a unit, enables one, or takes one away.
A unit no link of akasha's reaches is weighed by nothing here.
Nothing here reads a page that is not a workstation service's.
Which files a service reaches is asked here by nothing at all.
Nothing here throws out of the landing.
A unit's fields are read flat rather than under the section each sits in.
A service a refused systemctl left as it was is put right by `akasha deploy`.
Nothing here starts a service, arms a timer, or moves a tree.
What composes a unit's text sits in no service's deploy closure, so writing it starts no deploy.

definition: the workstation units kept as their pages state them
